# Photo quality check card

## Purpose
Runs before the gate model and rejects photos that are unusable for simple pixel reasons: too small, too dark or too bright. It does not look at what is in the photo, and it does not check sharpness or framing. A rejected photo gets a specific message (for example "too dark, try again in daylight") and no model runs. The module and its tests are `quality/photo_quality.py` and `tests/test_photo_quality.py`; it is not wired into any backend.

## Settings
`models/quality/quality_rules.yaml`, status "provisional" (as in the file below), reproduced as committed:

```yaml
# Photo quality rules, run before the gate model. All values are DESIGN parameters and PROVISIONAL:
# they have not been validated on phone photos (none were available). The next step sets them from
# validation images by a rule fixed in advance.
quality:
  status: provisional
  min_side_px: 224            # the models take 224x224 input
  analysis_max_side: 512      # the image is shrunk to this before measuring, so the blur measure is comparable
  dark_mean: 40.0             # mean grey level (0-255) below this is too dark
  bright_mean: 225.0          # mean grey level above this is too bright
  blur_laplacian_var: 0       # blur check switched off: failed the pre-registered criteria (docs/photo_quality_check.md, results/quality/pass2.txt)
```

The darkness, brightness and minimum-size values are placeholders chosen without looking at data. They are not calibrated. The blur check is switched off (`blur_laplacian_var: 0`).

## What was measured
Source: `results/quality/pass2.json` and `pass2.txt`, run as pre-registered in `docs/photo_quality_check.md`, on the disease validation (625 images) and test (631 images) sets. Degradations are synthetic and are not real phone failures.

| | Validation | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Originals rejected | 24 of 625 | 11 of 631 |
| Darkened to 20% flagged too dark | 625 of 625 | 630 of 631 |
| Glare +150 flagged too bright | 483 of 625 | 502 of 631 |

The rejected originals were rejected for being under the minimum side (validation 6, test 2) or, before the blur check was switched off, for blur. No original was rejected for darkness or brightness. The glare degradation (adding 150 to every pixel) is not a physical glare model, so the 77 to 80% figure shows only how the brightness limit reacts to it.

## The blur check and why it is off
The blur limit (variance of the Laplacian below 30) was tested against criteria fixed beforehand and failed them on the validation split: it rejected 0.0288 of sharp originals, against a limit of 0.02 (it caught 0.9920 of radius-4 copies, which met its criterion). The check is therefore switched off, and sharpness is reported as not reliably measurable on this data. This was a near miss, not a clear failure. A first calibration pass using percentile limits was rejected earlier (`results/quality/calibration.txt`). Laplacian variance depends on resolution and content, and none of this transfers to phone photos.

## Limitations
- Studio-style images only. No phone photo was available, so the module has never been tried on real photos.
- Does not check sharpness or framing. A blurry or badly framed maize leaf can pass.
- A leaf that fills the frame cannot be measured by a green-pixel share without rejecting yellow, nutrient-deficient leaves, so no such check exists.
- The test split was used twice for quality reports. No model is tuned on it.
- A blurry or dark photo tends to produce low-confidence model results, which fusion treats as not assessed. This was not measured.
